27/06/2020

Dr Robert Edwards
Neurologist
Rushford Hospital
765 Long Gully Road
Littletown

Dear Dr Edwards,
RE: Ms Sarah Day               DOB: 29/07/1997

Thank you for seeing Ms Day, a 20-year-old university student, who presented with unilateral headache associated with neurological signs. She requires your neurological assessment and management.

Ms Day has a stressful part-time job. She smokes and drinks alcohol moderately. She has no family history of migraine, and she takes oral contraceptive regularly.

Ms Day has a three-month history of repeated attacks of unilateral, occipital- temporal headache extending to the vertex for the past three months. The pain is steady and  associated with anxiety, dizziness, balance loss, nausea and visual disturbance without any clear trigger factors, and it lasts for one to two days. Her initial examination was normal. Therefore, she was advised on relaxation techniques and sleep regime and commenced on metoclopramide and paracetamol during the attacks. 
Over the past two months, Ms Day`s episodes have been more severe and frequent. In addition, she has had a neck pain and depression. Subsequently, eletripan and ibuprofen were prescribed on 04/01/2018, and amitriptyline was added three weeks later.

Today, Ms Day complained of numbness and tingling sensation over the fourth and fifth fingers of the left hand. She reported a car accident with a whiplash injury in June 2017. Based on these finding, I am referring Ms Day to you for further investigation and treatment. 
For any queries, please do not hesitate to contact me.
Yours sincerely,

Doctor
